why: a conditional expression reads its condition, then the selected operand only; a same-file call that changes its argument inside an operand changes it only when that operand is selected (design/heap-stage5.md section 3). The heap core reads both sides of note, route, stray, doubled and skewed (the world threaded through the arm taken): note returns the call from one operand where the candidate returns it from an if (proved); route is a nested ternary with the call in two operands against two ifs (proved); stray records at a non-positive count where the parent records nothing (unproved, WITNESS); doubled passes the ternary as an argument (proved); skewed records on both paths where the parent records only when the flag is off (unproved, WITNESS). The candidates of tally, ladder and leak assign in an if without a return, which the heap core does not read, so both sides take the value reading, where the arm taken carries the changed counter out: tally reads the counter after a ternary (proved); ladder passes a nested ternary as an argument (proved); leak changes the counter on both paths in the candidate (unproved, WITNESS); plain and the callees are untouched. The short-circuit operators are the conditional they are (ECMA-262 13.13): the right operand of &&, || and ?? runs only when the left does not decide, so a same-file call there changes its argument only then. noted returns && of a record call against an if, named ?? of one against an if (heap core, proved); gated (&&), spare (||) and fallback (??) bind the operator's value and read the counter after it against an assignment in an if (value reading, proved); slipped changes the counter on both paths in the candidate (unproved, WITNESS); anchor reads a found slot's id or one a call attaches to the unit's list (`found?.id ?? attach(xs, ..)`, the shape of a find-or-attach) against an if that returns (proved); orphan attaches on both paths in the candidate (unproved, WITNESS); guard tests && as an if's condition against two nested ifs (proved); lazy writes `ok ||= bump(c, by) > 1`, a logical assignment that short-circuits as || does (ECMA-262 13.15.2), against an if (proved); attach is untouched.
